summary: Framing pass on Global/Latest (the serialized ADocument graph) across all six Revit 2026 samples. Established the primitive encodings (AString = u32 charcount + UTF-16LE; ElementId = int64 LE, invalid = -1; GUID = 16 raw bytes; class ref = u16 schema type id; typed pointer = i32 -1 + u16 classId; bool = byte), decoded the byte-identical 0x53-byte prologue and the following head structures (m_storedByRevitBuild build strings, a 163-entry GUID-keyed 'Autodesk Revit' service/app map, a u32-keyed table of typed manager objects, a typed null-pointer run, the m_oNobleSecondaryData block with 86 ColorFillSecondaryData entries carrying real ElemTable ElementIds), and mapped the whole stream into byte regions. The single biggest finding: 30-60% of every non-DACH Global/Latest is the Autodesk Forge units/spec schema JSON dictionary — ~590 clean (typeid, json) AString pairs followed by a ~0.5-1 MB compressed continuation whose codec (0xff-flagged length prefixes, 0xffXX flagged literals, byte-shifted LZ back-references) is the same phenomenon as the 'corrupted' tail of Formats/Latest. Wrote a reusable parser/region-mapper with heuristic class-ordinal, GUID and ElementId scanners, plus the spec doc and an inbox note.
key_findings: 8-byte raw stream prefix is `05 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` (u64 5) in ALL six files; gzip member starts at raw offset 8; a 106-797-byte un-decoded tail follows the deflate stream (632 in racbasic).

The first 0x53 inflated bytes are byte-identical across all six samples: u32 28 (=ADocument type id) then typed-pointer tokens (i32 -1, u16 classId) resolving to 935 ContentTable and 416 AppInfoManager, two ElementId64 -1 (m_ownerFamilyId, m_ownerFamilyContainingGroupId), DevBranchInfo {1, 2662} where 2662 == ADocument's schema version, 3 bool bytes, u32 0 = m_executedUpgrades count.

Encodings verified: AString = u32 char count + UTF-16LE (e.g. 0e 00 00 00 'Autodesk Revit' @0x3df); ElementId = int64 LE, invalid = 8x0xff (99859 = 13 86 01 00 00 00 00 00 @0x46e7, same u64 keys a 40-byte record in Global/ElemTable @0xce6e); GUID = 16 raw bytes (163 entries sorted by raw bytes => std::map); class refs are u16 Formats/Latest type ids (0x32a = 810 = ColorFillSecondaryData in every object header).

Head layout after the prologue: u32 count + AStrings = m_storedByRevitBuild (Revit build history), then an object headed (-1, class 0x644, 1, count) with 163/52/121/180/305/1243 entries of {u32 1, GUID, AString 'Autodesk Revit', ElementId64 -1, u32 803, u32 833, i32 -1, u32 n, n x (u32 key, u32 val)} = m_oExServicesUsed-like external-service/app registry.

Next: `u32 1, u32 0xf1` (constant in every file) then a u32-keyed table (keys 2..17x) whose values are u16 class ids of document-level manager objects (0x475 DBViewInfo, 0x464 DBDrawingInfo, 0x1ad AppearanceInfo, 0x1a ADocWarnings) followed by their mostly-zero inline bodies; then 8 typed null pointers (742 CategoryTable, 426 AppearanceAssetTable, ...).

m_oNobleSecondaryData: 'NobleDocWarnings' object + 86 ColorFillSecondaryData entries in racbasic (9 with explicit ff ff ff ff 2a 03 01 00 00 00 headers, matching the declared u32 9; the rest embedded), each with strings (group/kind/scheme name) and ElementId64s (99859, 99860, 99861, 99864, 102898...) all present in Global/ElemTable.

The middle ~57% of racbasic (853,525 B; 525 KB-1 MB in the others) is the Autodesk Forge units/spec JSON dictionary: pre-header (u64 elementId 0xc3e83, i64 -1, u64 1, i64 -1, u32 1, u32 893 declared entries) then (typeid AString, json AString) pairs stored verbatim (589 in racbasic, 0 in rme) followed by a compressed continuation of the same JSON; dach has no units dictionary.

The compression is real, not corruption: rme's first entry has length prefix `26 ff ff ff` (flag | 38 chars) and JSON code units with high byte 0xff (`22 ff`='\"', `20 ff`=' ', `69 ff`='i') whose low bytes reproduce racbasic's plain JSON exactly; deeper in, literal runs at odd/even byte offsets with dropped substrings indicate a byte-oriented LZ codec. The same signature explains the 'intrinsically corrupted' tail of Formats/Latest reported by schema-a (inbox note filed).

Class-ordinal statistics: the reliable signal is (i32 -1, u16 X, u32 0|1) tokens (top X in racbasic: 810 ColorFillSecondaryData x9, then singletons 935 ContentTable, 416 AppInfoManager, 4198, 4088, 2793, 1604, 742 CategoryTable, 426 AppearanceAssetTable, 237 AnalyticalAutomationEditModeMgr); the most frequent raw u16/u32 values in the 0x100-0x1400 range are round numbers (0x100 x555, 0x200, 0xa00, 0xb00, 0xe00...) that are enums/flags, not class ids. My independent schema token scan (rank+12) matches schema_a.json names exactly for ids <= ~1450.

Global/Latest holds no element geometry: it is document-level tables/settings, the app/service registry, secondary NOBLE data, the units-schema dictionary and a tail of named settings objects (numbering schemas, DB server 'Revit Default DB Server', RbsSystem defaults, RevisionSettings per view class, LB_* link tables, room names). The BasicFileInfo document GUID does not occur anywhere in the stream.
confidence: HIGH for the primitive encodings (AString, ElementId64, GUID, class-ref u16, constant prologue, build-string list, GUID-map entry framing, ElemTable cross-check) and for the region boundaries in all six files; MEDIUM for the identification of the middle blob as the compressed continuation of the Forge units JSON dictionary and for the NobleSecondaryData / u32-keyed table framing; LOW for the exact ADocument field-to-token mapping above prologue offset 0x34, for the semantics of the GUID-map integers and the 0xf1 constant, and for class-name resolution of ids >= ~1450 (schema tail not decoded).
open_questions: What do the 8-byte raw stream prefix (u64 5 in all six) and the 106-797-byte post-deflate raw tail mean?

Exact prologue token-to-ADocument-field mapping above 0x34: which (-1, cls) token is m_pStyleSettings vs m_pHistory vs m_pSteelModelInfo vs m_pPartitionTable, and what are the interleaved u32 0/1 words (m_pHostDocument? present/refcount flags?).
Semantics of the GUID-keyed 'Autodesk Revit' map (external services vs add-in/updater registry) and of its per-entry u32s 803/826/833/842/844/846 and (key,value) pairs.

Meaning of the constant `u32 1, u32 0xf1` and the u32-keyed typed-object table (keys 2..17x): a document singleton/manager registry? Requires class-name resolution of u16 ids in the un-decoded schema tail (0x600-0x11e9).

The units-JSON compression codec (flagged 0xffffffXX length prefixes, 0xffXX flagged literal code units, byte-shifted LZ back-reference runs) — decoding it recovers ~30-60% of every Global/Latest and likely the tail of Formats/Latest as well.

Framing of the ~100-150 KB secondary-data gap (browser organization, view/sheet name records, MEP space/electrical naming schemes, WireSizes.xml) and of the tail region (12-wide vectors, LB_* link tables, room/name records with doubles).

Whether the declared units count 893 is honoured across the compressed part (implies ~250-370 compressed entries per file) and whether dach's much larger tail carries an equivalent structure without the units JSON.
next_steps: Crack the units-JSON / Formats-tail text codec (dedicated 'units-codec' agent): start from rme entry 1 where flagged literals mask cleanly, then handle the byte-shifted back-reference runs; validate by regenerating racbasic's 589 plain entries from a compressed file.

Feed schema_a.json field lists into global_latest.py to decode object bodies field-by-field (ColorFillSecondaryData, NOBLE_PrimaryDataId, DBViewInfo, AppearanceInfo) and settle the u32-keyed table semantics.
Resolve class ids >= 0x48a by decoding the compressed tail of Formats/Latest (same codec); then rename the prologue pointers (4198/4088/2793) and the keyed-table classes definitively.
Frame the 100-150 KB NOBLE secondary-data gap and the tail region record-by-record (RevisionSettings pairs, LB_* tables, room records), reusing the AString/ElementId64 anchors.
Decode the raw-stream post-deflate trailer (TRACKER A10) and the meaning of the 8-byte prefix (compare with the other Global/* streams' prefixes 00/01).
Merge the ElemTable record-layout hint (40-byte records, id repeated twice, 0x189 shared with the GUID map) from docs/inbox/global-latest.md into the A4 elem-table work.
